drivingQuestion: Which candles and scents are made for their light or fragrance, so that the havdala blessing may be recited over them?
outcomeNote: The principle that only a scent made for fragrance gets a blessing survives the objection from the perfumer's shop, and R' Yosei's reason is explained as a majority argument; the remaining rulings and baraitot are recorded without dispute.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כֹּל שֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין לְפָנָיו בַּיּוֹם וּבַלַּיְלָה — אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו. וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין מוֹצִיאִין לְפָנָיו אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה — מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: And «Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said: Any» deceased «before whom» a candle «is taken out» both «by day and by night,» it is evident that the candle is for the purpose of honoring the deceased; therefore, «one may not recite a blessing over it. And any» deceased «before whom» a candle «is taken out only by night,» it is evident that the purpose of the candle is for its light alone, and «one may recite a blessing over it.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא, וְשֶׁמֶן הֶעָשׂוּי לְהַעֲבִיר אֶת הַזּוּהֲמָא — אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rav Huna said: Over spices» used to deodorize «the bathroom and» fragrant «oil» intended «to remove filth, one may not recite a blessing» as they are not used for their pleasant fragrance.

segments.he: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא עֲבִידָא לָא מְבָרְכִין עִלָּוֵיהּ? מֵתִיבִי: הַנִּכְנָס לַחֲנוּתוֹ שֶׁל בַּשָּׂם וְהֵרִיחַ רֵיחַ, אֲפִילּוּ יָשַׁב שָׁם כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ אֶלָּא פַּעַם אַחַת. נִכְנַס וְיָצָא, נִכְנַס וְיָצָא — מְבָרֵךְ עַל כׇּל פַּעַם וּפַעַם. וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא, וְקָמְבָרֵךְ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that to say» that «any» case «where it is not used for its» pleasant «fragrance, one may not recite a blessing over it?» The Gemara «raises an objection» based on the Tosefta: «One who enters the store of a perfumer, and smelled a fragrance, even if he sat there throughout the entire day, he only recites a blessing once.» However, «if one entered and exited, entered and exited, he recites a blessing on each and every occasion. Isn’t» it a case «here, where» the spices «are not intended for fragrance,» as they are not used to improve the scent in the store, «and,» nevertheless, «one recites a blessing?»

segments.he: אִין, לְרֵיחָא נָמֵי הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנֵירְחוּ אִינָשֵׁי וְנֵיתוּ וְנִזְבּוֹן מִינֵּיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Yes,» in this case the spices «are also intended for fragrance;» they are used to generate a scent in the store «so that people will smell» them «and come and purchase from him.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְהֵרִיחַ רֵיחַ, אִם רוֹב נׇכְרִים — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, אִם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְבָרֵךְ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — נָמֵי אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַטְּרוֹת לִכְשָׁפִים.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «One who was walking outside a city and smelled a scent; if the majority» of the town’s residents «are gentiles he may not recite a blessing» over the scent, but «if the majority are Jews, he may recite a blessing. Rabbi Yosei says: Even if the majority are Jews, one may not recite a blessing, as the daughters of Israel burn incense to witchcraft» and the spices were certainly made for witchcraft, not for their fragrance.

segments.he: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ לִכְשָׁפִים מְקַטְּרָן?! — הָוֵה לַהּ מִיעוּטָא לִכְשָׁפִים, וּמִיעוּטָא נָמֵי לְגַמֵּר אֶת הַכֵּלִים. אִשְׁתְּכַח רוּבָּא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא עֲבִיד, וְכׇל רוּבָּא דְּלָאו לְרֵיחָא עֲבִיד לָא מְבָרֵךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that to say that they all burn incense to witchcraft?» Rather, «there is a minority» of people who burn incense «to witchcraft, and a» different «minority» who burn spices in order «to perfume» their «garments with incense. A majority,» therefore, exists that «does not use it for fragrance, and in a case where the majority does not use it for fragrance, one does not recite a blessing.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַמְהַלֵּךְ בְּעַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת בִּטְבֶרְיָא וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת בְּצִפּוֹרִי וְהֵרִיחַ רֵיחַ, אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחֶזְקָתוֹ אֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי אֶלָּא לְגַמֵּר בּוֹ אֶת הַכֵּלִים.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who walks on Shabbat eve in Tiberias» or «at the conclusion of Shabbat in Tzippori, and smelled the scent» of incense «may not recite a blessing, as the presumption is» that «it was intended to perfume garments.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בַּשּׁוּק שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִתְרַצָּה לְהָרִיחַ — הֲרֵי זֶה חוֹטֵא.
segments.en: On a related note, the Gemara cites the following: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «One who was walking in the marketplace of idolators and willingly smelled» the incense wafting there, «he is a sinner,» as he should not have the intention to smell it.

segments.he: וְאֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַנֵּר עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹתוּ.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And one does not recite the blessing over the candle until he derives benefit» from its light.

moves.summary: Rav (via Rav Yehuda): a candle carried before the deceased by day and night gets no blessing; one carried only at night does
moves.about: the mishna's rule against blessing over the candle of the dead applies to a candle carried before the deceased by day and by night, not to one carried only at night, which is for light

moves.summary: Rav Huna: no blessing over bathroom spices or oil made to remove filth
moves.about: the mishna's exclusion of the spices of the dead extends to any scent not used for its fragrance: bathroom spices and oil made to remove filth

moves.summary: Is that to say that no scent not made for fragrance gets a blessing?
moves.about: the perfumer's scent is not made to perfume the shop, yet one blesses over it — against the principle drawn from Rav Huna that a scent not made for fragrance gets no blessing

moves.summary: Objection from the baraita: one blesses in a perfumer's shop, though its scent is not made to perfume the shop
moves.about: Rav Huna's ruling implies the general principle that no blessing is recited over any scent not made for its fragrance

moves.summary: Yes: the perfumer's scent is also for fragrance, so that people smell it and come to buy
moves.about: the objection from the perfumer's shop: its scent is also made for fragrance, so that people smell it and come to buy

moves.summary: The baraita: a scent smelled outside a town gets a blessing only if the town's majority is Jewish
moves.about: the baraita on one who smells a scent outside a town: the blessing depends on whether the majority is gentile or Jewish; R' Yosei forbids even with a Jewish majority

moves.summary: R' Yosei: even with a Jewish majority no blessing, since the daughters of Israel burn incense for witchcraft
moves.about: whether one blesses over a scent smelled outside a town whose majority is Jewish

moves.summary: Do they all burn incense for witchcraft?!
moves.about: R' Yosei's reason overreaches: surely not all the daughters of Israel burn incense for witchcraft

moves.summary: A minority for witchcraft plus a minority for perfuming garments make a majority not for fragrance, and over such a majority one does not bless
moves.about: R' Yosei means that a minority burning incense for witchcraft together with a minority perfuming garments make a majority not for fragrance, over which one does not bless

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan (via R' Ḥiyya bar Abba): a scent on Shabbat eve in Tiberias or motzaei Shabbat in Tzippori gets no blessing, being presumed for perfuming garments
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's ruling: one who smells a scent on Shabbat eve in Tiberias or at the conclusion of Shabbat in Tzippori does not bless, since it is presumed to be for perfuming garments

moves.summary: The baraita: one who willingly smells the incense in an idolaters' market is a sinner
moves.about: the baraita: one who walks in an idolaters' market and willingly smells the incense is a sinner

moves.cueHe: ואין מברכין על הנר עד שיאותו
moves.summary: The mishna's next lemma: no blessing over the candle until one derives benefit from its light
moves.about: the mishna's next lemma: one does not bless over the candle until he derives benefit from its light
